analysis.title: AI Correction: Multiples Reset, Estimates Hold
key_insights: The AI & Tech Diffusion index fell 26.6% from 30 Sep to the 5 Nov close versus -3.7% for MSCI ACWI. Carried to the 6 Nov close for Japanese and Asian listings, the portfolio fell 28.4% (ACWI -4.3%) and is 33% below its 6 Oct peak. The decline came in two legs: mid-October, and late October deepening after the 3 Nov US elections.

Multiple compression accounts for more than the entire decline. Across 91 members with positive FY2 EPS, consensus EPS rose about 3 log points in every region while P/E multiples contracted about 37 log points overall (26 to 48 across regions).

Of 94 members, 61 had reported by their cut-offs and their FY2 estimates rose (median +4.5%, net revision breadth +57%). The 33 not yet captured show median FY2 EPS revision of +0.3% and net breadth of +29%. Seven reported after their cut-off and 26 had not reported since 30 Sep.

The US and Europe moved from mid-range to the bottom quintile of their post-2019 NTM P/E ranges (median percentiles 17 and 13). Japan de-rated most, from the 82nd to the 28th percentile, even though every Japanese member saw flat or higher FY2 estimates. Asia/EM remains near its median (53rd).
Asia/EM has the highest share of downgrades: 7 of 26 members (27%) saw FY2 consensus cut by more than 0.5% over the four weeks to the cut-off.

Stress test: a hypothetical 20% cut to NTM EPS would push 55% of members above their own median P/E, versus 27% today. A 20% cut lifts P/E by 25% at a fixed price. The report states this is not a forecast of earnings cuts.

Median break-even EPS cut (the cut that lifts P/E to its own median) is about 24% in the US, 23% in Europe and 16% in Japan. In Asia/EM 14 of 26 members already trade above their own median, so the median break-even is below zero.

On a 13-to-24-month horizon (NNTM) the median break-even cut rises from 16% to about 21%. Asia/EM moves from no cushion to about 18%, and Europe's cushion falls below Japan's. Median NNTM/NTM growth is about 28%, highest in Asia/EM at 33%, and 73% of members show growth above their own norm, which may be vulnerable to delays in AI infrastructure investment.

From 30 Sep to the cut-off, AI Adopters returned -3.2% and AI Enablers -29.0%, a gap of about 26 percentage points. After beta adjustment (1.38 Adopters, 1.63 Enablers) Adopters are +2.7% and Enablers -22.0%. The Adopters/Enablers ratio made its largest move of this length since 2019, and the two indices are level year to date.

The rotation is valuation-led, not earnings-led. Enablers' median NTM P/E fell from 27.4x to 18.6x, close to Adopters at 18.1x. Enablers retain stronger revisions (net breadth +48% versus +2% for Adopters), and 35% of Adopters have seen FY2 cuts since 30 Sep.

Among reporters, the tercile with the largest FY2 upgrades (median +7.9%) fell 37 log points versus 9 for the lowest-revision tercile (rank correlation -0.42). MS says this is consistent with, but does not establish, investors discounting capex-related upgrades.

Capex-heavy reporters (33 names) de-rated about 40 log points versus about 25 for other reporters. Holding EPS revisions constant, a 10% rise in capex estimates was associated with about 4 percentage points of relative underperformance the next trading day (t-stat -2.8, 31 names). Across all reporters the capex association is not significant, and MS calls it an ex-post association, not causal.

Macro uncertainty from the Iran conflict and energy volatility may have amplified the correction. Rising yields are a separate risk to valuations, since they could compress multiples further even if estimates hold.

MS recommends selectivity over indiscriminate dip-buying: reduce concentration in capex-sensitive upstream AI names, broaden selectively toward Adopters with resilient earnings expectations, and prioritise US and European valuation cushions.

What would change the view: deteriorating revisions among capex-sensitive Enablers would strengthen the case for reducing upstream exposure. Improving Adopters earnings momentum would support the downstream rotation. Sustained upstream upgrades would temper the case for further reductions.

sector_views.rationale: Avoid indiscriminate dip-buying and reduce concentration. Data-centre regulation and project delays could weaken orders and earnings, though Enablers still show stronger revisions.
Selective broadening toward Adopters with resilient earnings expectations. Their outperformance is valuation-led and earnings confirmation is still needed.

earnings_insights: Reporting-season FY2 EPS revisions are positive: 61 of 94 members reported with median FY2 revision +4.5% and net breadth +57%. The 33 not yet captured show median +0.3% and net breadth +29%. These are consensus revisions, not company results.
Enablers' net revision breadth over four weeks to the cut-off is +48% versus +2% for Adopters, and 35% of Adopters have seen FY2 estimate cuts since 30 Sep.
risk_factors: Consensus estimates may not yet reflect potential delays to AI infrastructure investment or tighter data-centre regulation.
Renewed upward pressure on yields could drive further multiple compression even if earnings estimates hold.
Above-normal growth expectations (73% of members above their own norm) are vulnerable to delays in AI infrastructure investment.
Iran conflict and energy market volatility may add to risk aversion.
33 members' latest results are not captured, so revisions may change as they report.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 tracks the AI & Tech Diffusion, AI Enablers and AI Adopters indices with ACWI, each rebased to 100 at end-June. Enablers fell with AI & Tech Diffusion while Adopters held their level.
Exhibit 5 shows the share of members above their own median P/E after hypothetical NTM EPS cuts of 10%, 20% and 30%, by region.
vol_and_positioning: Asia/EM has the highest share of FY2 downgrades (27% of members) and more than half of its members already trade above their own median NTM P/E, so it has no median valuation cushion.
The US and Europe sit in the bottom quintile of their post-2019 NTM P/E ranges (median percentiles 17 and 13). Japan is at the 28th percentile and Asia/EM at the 53rd.
geopolitical: Uncertainty surrounding the Iran conflict and energy market volatility may have added to broader risk aversion.
The 3 Nov US elections preceded a deepening of the second leg of the AI sell-off.

tension_points.bull_case: Consensus FY2 EPS rose about 3 log points in every region while multiples fell about 37 log points. 61 reporters saw median FY2 upgrades of +4.5%, and US and European AI stocks sit in the bottom quintile of their post-2019 NTM P/E ranges.
tension_points.bear_case: Consensus may not yet reflect delays to AI infrastructure investment or data-centre regulation. The names with the largest upgrades fell most, and a hypothetical 20% EPS cut would push 55% of members above their own median P/E.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Deteriorating consensus revisions among capex-sensitive Enablers, especially among the 33 constituents not yet captured, would strengthen the bear case. Sustained upstream upgrades would temper it.

tension_points.bull_case: Adopters outperformed Enablers by about 26 percentage points since 30 Sep, and beta explains little of it. The ratio made its largest move of this length since 2019.
tension_points.bear_case: The rotation is valuation-led. Enablers retain stronger revisions (+48% versus +2% net breadth) and 35% of Adopters have seen FY2 cuts.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Improving Adopters earnings momentum would support the rotation. Deteriorating Enabler revisions would strengthen the case for reducing upstream exposure.

theme_stances.key_argument: Avoid indiscriminate dip-buying because AI multiples have reset but investors may be pricing future earnings risks not yet reflected in consensus revisions.
theme_stances.evidence: Avoid indiscriminate dip-buying: AI multiples have reset

theme_stances.key_argument: Adopters' resilience supports diversification from capex-sensitive stocks, but stronger earnings confirmation is needed.
